policy_facts.text: Managers and directors can see the profile and time-off balance of people in their reporting chain. Access depends on who is signed in, not on who someone says they are. If you're not in the person's reporting chain, the record can't be shared.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: You can see all of your own records. Managers and directors can see the profile and time-off balance of people in their reporting chain, and can run the compliance check on their PTO requests. Your benefits elections and your HR tickets are private to you and HR. Nobody else can see your records. If you ask about someone else's records and you are not in their reporting chain, the answer is that the record can't be shared. Access is based on who you are, not on who you say you are: tools that show HR records check the person signed in. Colleagues on the same team, peers and people in other reporting lines cannot see each other's records, even with good intentions. If a colleague asks you for information from their own record, point them to the HR Portal, where they can see it themselves.
